drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna teach נרה at all, once it has taught הובירה?
outcomeNote: The question is posed and left standing here; it is answered in the following unit.

segments.he: הָיְתָה שְׁנַת שִׁדָּפוֹן כּוּ׳. הַשְׁתָּא הוֹבִירָהּ עוֹלָה לוֹ, נָרָהּ מִיבַּעְיָא?
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: If one of the two years after the sale «was a year of blight,» the buyer is entitled to an additional year’s crops. If the buyer plowed the field but did not sow it, or if he left it fallow, that year counts as part of his tally, as it was fit to produce a crop. The Gemara asks: «Now» that it was taught that if the buyer «left» his field «fallow» that year «counts» as part of «his» tally, even though he did not cultivate the field at all, «is it necessary» for the mishna to teach that the year counts as part of his tally if «he plowed» the field but did not sow it?

moves.summary: quotes the mishna clause of the earlier unit as the lemma
moves.about: the gemara quotes the mishna clause on years that count toward the tally

moves.cueHe: השתא הובירה עולה לו, נרה מיבעיא?
moves.summary: attacks the נרה clause as redundant given the הובירה clause
moves.about: why the mishna needed to state that a year in which the buyer plowed counts, once it has already said that a year left wholly fallow counts
